name: Render
summary: Render builds and deploys web services, background workers, cron jobs and managed Postgres and Key Value stores from your Git repo, all described in one `render.yaml` file if you like.
intro: You link a Git branch, and every push triggers a build and a deploy; you can also deploy a prebuilt Docker image. Each piece of your app is a service of a given type: a web service gets an `onrender.com` subdomain and must listen on `0.0.0.0` (port 10000 by default), a private service is reachable only on your private network, a background worker takes no incoming traffic and usually polls a queue, a cron job runs a command on a UTC cron schedule and is billed for how long it runs, and static sites are served from a CDN. Render also runs managed Render Postgres databases and Render Key Value instances, which run Valkey 8 when newly created and work with Redis clients.

A Blueprint is a `render.yaml` file in your repo that declares all of these together, with environment variables that point at each other: a web service can take `DATABASE_URL` from a database’s connection string. Deploys replace instances with zero downtime unless the service has a persistent disk, and if a build or pre-deploy command fails, the previous deploy keeps serving. Preview environments can spin up a copy of the stack for a pull request.

Billing combines a workspace plan (Hobby is $0, Pro $25 a month) with compute per instance, from $7 a month for 512 MB up to 12 CPUs and 96 GB. Web services, Postgres and Key Value also have Free instances for trying things out, with tight limits.
strengths: Push to deploy with zero-downtime rollouts, rollbacks and per-pull-request preview environments
One `render.yaml` describes services, workers, cron jobs, databases and shared environment groups, and wires their connection strings together
Managed Postgres with backups, read replicas and high availability, plus a Valkey-based Key Value store for caches and job queues
A free starting point: 750 Free instance hours per workspace each month for web services
limits: Free web services spin down after 15 minutes without traffic and take about a minute to come back; Free Postgres is capped at 1 GB and expires after 30 days
Filesystems are ephemeral; adding a persistent disk turns off zero-downtime deploys for that service, and cron jobs can’t use disks at all
Autoscaling on CPU or memory needs a Pro workspace or higher, and a service tops out at 100 instances (5 on the largest plans)
Free web services can’t scale past one instance, offer SSH access or receive private network traffic

story: Small teams that moved to AWS often found that the cloud came with a second job. Anurag Goel, Render’s founder and CEO, told TechCrunch in 2019 that startups had to hire expensive DevOps engineers or consultants to build their infrastructure, then keep patching it and managing security and access. Render launched in April 2019 as a managed cloud that “abstracts all of that away, and automates all of it”, while aiming to be “the easiest and most flexible provider for teams to run any application in the cloud.”

In October 2019 Render won the Startup Battlefield at TechCrunch Disrupt SF; TechCrunch described its automated deployments and app management as reminiscent of Heroku. By 2021 Goel said many customers were moving over from Heroku and AWS for features such as infrastructure as code, private networking and persistent storage, and the company announced plans for a free plan for web services and databases.

In June 2023 Render raised a $50 million Series B led by Bessemer Venture Partners. In February 2025 it switched newly created Render Key Value instances from Redis to Valkey, an open-source fork of Redis 7.2.4, while existing Redis instances kept running without further version updates.

choices.choice: A managed platform, not a thin layer over AWS
choices.why: Goel pitched Render as an alternative to AWS, Azure and Google Cloud for teams without DevOps staff, arguing that the big clouds “were built for the 2000s, when managing infrastructure was the norm at every company.”

choices.choice: The whole stack as code in the repo
choices.why: Blueprints put services, databases and environment groups in one `render.yaml`, which Goel listed among the modern features drawing customers from Heroku and AWS.
Launched in 2020, they spin up disposable copies of the stack so developers, QA and product teams can test a change in an environment that looks like production.
